correctness.rationale: For gradients g1=g0+δ,g2=g0−δ, the ball max-min objective equals <g0,d>−|<δ,d>|. Since a>b, <δ,g0>=(a²−b²)/4>0 and the weaker g2 linear branch supports the ball until its optimizer reaches <δ,d>=0. Evaluating the support vector gives d=g0+R g2/b and the exact c_cd, c_bal radii. At the balanced branch the unique best point of the ball-hyperplane intersection lies in direction of h=proj_{δ^⊥}g0, yielding the stated square-root formula. Squaring positive ratios and simplifying gives c_bal<1 iff ρ<(3q²−1)/(2q); when q≤1/3 this is outside the allowed non-antiparallel interval. Equal norms force δ⊥g0, so d=(1+c)g0. Independent 120 randomly chosen harmful geometric configurations, with seven radii each, matched a dense 3001-point scalar-dual envelope to 1e−5 relative; threshold signs and exact inequalities verified algebraically. No convergence of nonlinear trajectories claimed.
residual_risks: Numerical dual checks are finite corroboration; exact support-plane and algebraic inequalities are the general argument.

originality.rationale: The foundational CAGrad theorem already supplies the general implicit simplex-dual optimizer, which is fully credited. The submitted claim isolates a nontrivial exact two-task active-to-balanced branch transition, common-descent zero crossing, and a sharp weaker-gradient norm ratio obstruction inside c<1. The later primary papers use different objectives or clipped/weighted variants. No read source explicitly supplies these radius boundaries and their safe-range ordering.
residual_risks: Because the original Lemma A.2 is an exact general variational representation, the new formulas can be derived by two-variable convex geometry; novelty is the evaluated piecewise phase boundary, not the abstract minimax identity.
Unindexed pedagogical derivations of this special case remain a possible coverage risk.

value.rationale: Separates two operationally distinct mathematical events: restoration of simultaneous first-order descent and exact equal task improvement. The sharp q≤1/3 safe-radius obstruction provides a natural regime in which CAGrad can improve both objectives without equalizing them. A useful explicit geometric classification of an established optimizer even though not a new algorithm or global theorem.
residual_risks: No guarantee of finite-step nonlinear objective improvement at arbitrary step sizes, practical training gain, or convergence to a Pareto target is claimed.

limitations: Pointwise first-order and noncollinear harmful-mean regime only; no assertion for other multiobjective geometries or clipped/weighted CAGrad.
The source convergence range c<1 concerns average loss; do not conflate with immediate decrease of every nonlinear task loss.
